autor: Louis IV the Bavarian (king of the Romans 1314, emperor 1328, d. 1347); the chapter on poverty drafted by Friars Minor at his court
quelle: Monumenta Germaniae Historica, Legum sectio IV: Constitutiones et acta publica imperatorum et regum, tom. V, ed. Iacobus Schwalm (Hannover and Leipzig: Hahn, 1909–1913), nr. 909 (Forma prior), pp. 722–745, and nr. 910, pp. 753–754. Internet Archive, monumentagerma05geseuoft. Public domain.
hinweis: The appeal survives in two forms: a first form that Friars Minor seem to have drafted for the king (nr. 909) and a second revised in the royal chancery (nr. 910); both carry the chapter on poverty. The excerpts are from the first form, read from the page images of Schwalm's edition, with his spelling; his apparatus of variants is not carried, and cuts are marked […]. Date and place are those of the chancery form. The English is this site's working translation (CC0).

sections.blurb: The opening of the appeal: John 'who calls himself pope' is an enemy of peace who thrives on the German civil war and condemns the empire's loyal Italians as heretics, 'one of the keys going wholly astray in him'.

units.orig: Nos Ludwicus Dei gratia Romanorum rex semper augustus proponimus contra Iohannem qui se dicit papam vicesimum secundum, quod inimicus sit pacis et intendit ad discordias et scandala suscitanda non solum in Ytalia, quod notorium est, sed etiam in Alemania, suscitando prelatos et principes commovendo per nuncios frequentes et litteras et sollicitando, ut contra sacrum imperium et nos debeant gwerram movere et pro viribus rebellare. Et quod sit sator discordiarum et seminator zizanie inter Christi fideles, apparet manifeste. Nam publice dicere dicitur, quod quando inter reges mundi et principes est discordia, tunc papa est verus papa et timetur papa et quilibet timet eum et facit quidquid libet, ex hoc manifeste se convincens sitire effusionem sanguinis christiani. Maxime autem dicere dicitur, quod discordia principum, nobilium et populi Alemanie salus est et pax Rom(anorum) pontificum et ecclesie. Unde cum multiplicarentur in Alemania occasione electionum diversarum cedes, occisiones et vulnera et gwerre et sanguinis effusiones proh dolor innocentis, nunquam unam litteram vel qualemcunque nuncium misit ad obviandum predictis periculis atque malis, cum tamen multos haberet in partibus exactores et collectores pecuniarum pro ipso, quibus hoc committere sine aliquo suo onere potuisset, si voluisset vel sibi de hoc cura aliqua fuisset. Ostendens se per hoc contra doctrinam facere et vitam et exempla Christi, cuius vicarium se mentitur et dicit.
units.en: We, Louis, by the grace of God king of the Romans, ever augustus, set forth against John, who calls himself the twenty-second pope, that he is an enemy of peace and aims to stir up discord and scandal not only in Italy, which is notorious, but also in Germany, rousing prelates and moving princes by frequent envoys and letters, and urging them to make war on the holy empire and on us and to rebel with all their strength. And that he is a sower of discord and of tares among the faithful of Christ is plain. For he is said to say in public that when there is discord among the kings and princes of the world, then the pope is truly pope and is feared, and everyone fears him and does whatever he pleases; by which he plainly convicts himself of thirsting for the shedding of Christian blood. Above all he is said to say that the discord of the princes, nobles and people of Germany is the safety and the peace of the Roman pontiffs and of the Church. Hence, when killings, slaughter and wounds, wars and the shedding, alas, of innocent blood multiplied in Germany on account of the divided elections, he never sent a single letter or any envoy whatever to meet these dangers and evils, although he had many exactors and collectors of money for himself in those parts, to whom he could have entrusted this at no cost to himself, had he wished it or cared about it at all. By this he shows that he acts against the teaching, the life and the example of Christ, whose vicar he falsely says he is.
units.note: The 'divided elections' are those of October 1314, when one party of electors chose Louis of Bavaria and the other Frederick of Austria; the war between them was decided only at Mühldorf in 1322. John XXII held that the empire was vacant until the pope approved a king, claimed its administration for himself, and opened proceedings against Louis in October 1323. This 'third appeal' answers that first process. 'Iohannem qui se dicit papam', 'John, who calls himself pope': from its first line the appeal no longer grants him the title.

units.orig: Item actor omnis malitie factus simul et iudex omnino subvertit iudicium. Et tantum excecavit ipsum malitia publice et notorie, quod una clavium in ipso prorsus errante insontes, pios et innocentes, iustos atque fideles catholicos, sicut patet late et notorie, in tota Lambardia et in diversis Ytalie partibus tanquam Paterenos et hereticos condempnavit. Ita quod longe plures, si veritatem contineret sua prava et iniqua sentencia, heretici essent et hereticorum fautores, quam alii, cum generaliter omnes fideles imperii et devotos nulla alia causa obtenta, hoc ipso quod fideles sunt imperii, perperam et inique pronunciat Paterenos, non attendens, quod tunc manet Petri privilegium, ubi ex ipsius fertur equitate iudicium. Quod una autem clavium erret in ipso, patet, cum membra Christi facit et iudicat membra dyaboli et veros catholicos tanquam veros hereticos condempnat et punit. Ipse autem Phariseorum sibi assumens supercilium putat se absolvere quos Deus ligat et ligare quos Deus solvit, in hoc contra Deum et fidem catholicam et sacram scripturam et veritatem et iustitiam faciendo.
units.en: Further, having made himself at once the prosecutor of every malice and the judge, he overturns judgment altogether. And malice has blinded him so publicly and notoriously that, with one of the keys going wholly astray in him, he has condemned as Patarenes and heretics guiltless, pious and innocent men, just and faithful catholics, as is widely and notoriously known, in all Lombardy and in various parts of Italy. So that, if his crooked and unjust sentence held the truth, far more would be heretics and supporters of heretics than not, since he wrongly and unjustly pronounces Patarenes all the faithful and devoted of the empire in general, for no other cause found than that they are faithful to the empire; not heeding that Peter's privilege remains only where judgment is given according to Peter's justice. That one of the keys errs in him is plain, since he makes and judges the members of Christ members of the devil, and condemns and punishes true catholics as true heretics. Taking on the haughty brow of the Pharisees, he thinks he looses those whom God binds and binds those whom God looses, and in this acts against God and the catholic faith, holy scripture, truth and justice.
units.note: The Visconti of Milan and the other Ghibellines of Lombardy, the empire's allies, had been tried for heresy by the pope's legates in 1321 and 1322; 'Patarenes' was the old Italian name for Cathars. 'Peter's privilege remains wherever judgment is given according to his justice' is a sentence of Pope Leo the Great that the canonists repeated: the power of the keys binds only when it judges rightly. Here the key 'errs' in a judgment of persons. The Franciscan chapter on poverty below turns the same idea into a doctrine of the 'key of knowledge' (Sachs. Poverty [5]).

sections.titel: The chapter on the highest poverty
sections.blurb: Chapter 28, drafted by Franciscans at the king's court: the pope has risen against Christ, his mother and the apostles; Francis's rule was sealed by the stigmata, which no 'leaden bull' can undo; Ad conditorem and Quum inter nonnullos make John a heretic, because what one pope has defined by the key of knowledge no successor may revoke.

units.titel: Against Christ, his mother and the apostles
units.orig: Non suffecit autem sibi temporalis imperii iura attemptare, subvertere et in coronam nostram et in fideles imperii tam nequiter desevire, nisi et ipsum dominum Ihesum Christum, regem regum et dominum dominancium principem regum terre et eius sacratissimam matrem, que eiusdem voti et status cum filio in observancia paupertatis vixit, et sanctum apostolorum collegium ipsorum denigrando vitam et actus insurgeret et doctrinam ewangelicam de paupertate altissima in qua exemplaris perfectio exterioris vite ipsorum de pleno et perfecto mundi contemptu tanquam in fundamento immobili est firmata. Quod fundamentum non solum sua mala vita et a mundi contemptu aliena conatur evertere, set heretico dogmate et venenata doctrina in predicacionibus publicis et sollempnibus et variis assercionibus affirmando asseruit, Christum et apostolos habuisse bona temporalia in communi eo modo, quo alia collegia habent. Quod dictum est notorie hereticum et prophanum et contra ewangelii sacrum textum.
units.en: But it was not enough for him to assail and overturn the rights of the temporal empire and to rage so wickedly against our crown and against the faithful of the empire; he had also to rise up against the Lord Jesus Christ himself, king of kings and lord of lords, prince of the kings of the earth, and against his most holy mother, who lived with her son under the same vow and state in the observance of poverty, and against the holy college of the apostles, blackening their life and acts, and against the gospel teaching of the highest poverty, on which, as on an immovable foundation, the exemplary perfection of their outward life, of full and perfect contempt of the world, is set. This foundation he tries to overturn not only by his evil life, a stranger to contempt of the world, but by heretical dogma and poisoned teaching as well, having asserted in public and solemn sermons and in various statements that Christ and the apostles had temporal goods in common in the way other colleges have them. Which saying is notoriously heretical and profane and against the sacred text of the gospel.
units.note: Chapter 28 of the first form, which German scholarship calls the 'Spiritual excursus' (spiritualistischer Exkurs), turns a political appeal into a treatise on poverty. Its editor, Jakob Schwalm, and the scholars before him found its sentences agreeing with Bonagratia of Bergamo's appeal, with Olivi's questions and with Ubertino of Casale's treatise on the highest poverty; friars of Michael's party had reached Louis's court by the spring of 1324. The archbishop of Mainz wrote to the pope that August that the appeal had been 'fabricated and chewed over in Lombardy'. Mary vowed to poverty with her son is a Spiritual theme. 'In the way other colleges have them' is the friars' reading of what the pope had defined in November 1323 (Decr. Nonnullos [1]): that it is heresy to say Christ and the apostles had nothing, 'nor even in common'.

units.orig: Innumera enim sunt dicta sanctorum prophetarum predicencium Christi paupertatem altissimam, cuius renovator fuit principalis seraphicus vir Franciscus. Tota enim silva sacri ewangelii quoad Christi ortum, incolatum et exitum et dicta sanctorum doctorum discipulorum ipsorum apostolorum usque ad hec tempora omnia clamant, Christum et apostolos vixisse in altissima paupertate predicta, que consistit in nichil habendo civiliter in hoc mundo. Quod si queratur, quid vult dicere paupertas altissima, de qua apostolus dicit: 'Altissima paupertas eorum etc.', respondet Innocencius papa V.: 'Alta paupertas habere pauca propria propter Deum, alcior que nulla habet propria, habet tamen in suo collegio in communi, altissima que nichil habet in hoc mundo in proprio vel communi, et hec fuit Christi et apostolorum'. In hoc immobili fundamento almus Christi confessor Franciscus pater eiusdem ordinis ordinem fundavit et sancta mater ecclesia regulam, quam Christo sibi revelante conposuit, approbavit et confirmavit et per plures Romanos pontifices, videlicet Honorium, Gregorium IX, Alexandrum quartum, Innocentium quartum, Innocencium V. et Nycolaum tercium et quartum et per diversos alios pontifices declaravit, omnibus una et concordi voce dicentibus, quod hec est regula ewangelica Christi et apostolorum imitativa, que nichil habebat vel habet in hoc mundo proprium vel commune, set in rebus, quibus utebantur et utuntur, habebant et habent tantummodo simplicem facti usum.
units.en: For countless are the sayings of the holy prophets foretelling the highest poverty of Christ, whose chief renewer was the seraphic man Francis. The whole forest of the holy gospel, as to Christ's birth, sojourn and departure, and the sayings of the holy doctors, the disciples of the apostles themselves, down to these times, all cry out that Christ and the apostles lived in the said highest poverty, which consists in having nothing civilly in this world. If it is asked what is meant by the highest poverty of which the apostle says 'their highest poverty' and so on, Pope Innocent V answers: 'High poverty is to have a few things of one's own for God's sake; higher, that which has nothing of its own but has things in common in its college; highest, that which has nothing in this world, of its own or in common; and this was the poverty of Christ and the apostles.' On this immovable foundation the gracious confessor of Christ Francis, father of that order, founded the order; and holy mother Church approved and confirmed the rule, which he composed as Christ revealed it to him, and declared it through many Roman pontiffs, namely Honorius, Gregory IX, Alexander IV, Innocent IV, Innocent V and Nicholas III and IV, and through various other pontiffs, all saying with one concordant voice that this is the gospel rule, imitating Christ and the apostles, which had and has nothing in this world of its own or in common, but in the things they used and use had and have only the simple use of fact.
units.note: The apostle is Paul, 2 Corinthians 8:2 in the Vulgate ('altissima paupertas eorum'), where it is said of the churches of Macedonia. Innocent V (1276) was the Dominican Peter of Tarentaise; Schwalm could not find the saying in his works. The three degrees are the Franciscan scale: monks own in common, friars own nothing. The list of popes who 'declared' the rule is the chain of authority the friars set against John XXII, and 'the simple use of fact' is the formula of Exiit (Exiit [4]).

units.orig: Et ut regula beati Francisci ostenderetur vere a Deo exisse et non oporteret professores ipsius timere, ne perirent penuria, ad subvencionem paupertatis ipsius probata est multociens miraculose eidem tota mundi machina deservire, prout in vita ipsius per ecclesiam approbata plenius continetur. Et ut appareret evidenter presentibus et futuris, regulam a beato Francisco editam et ab ecclesia confirmatam esse vere illam, quam Christus apostolos docuit et in se ipso exemplo firmavit quoad hunc articulum, eandem regulam in suo actore Francisco dignatus est Ihesus Christus bullare stigmatibus sue sacratissime passionis. Unde et paucis elapsis diebus a condicione eiusdem regule meruit predictis stigmatibus insigniri, ut non presumeret homo mortalis evertere bulla plumbea, quod immortalis Deus regnans in celo sue passionis et crucis signaculis stabilivit. Et omnes Romani pontifices predecessores ipsius et plura generalia concilia cum multa devocione et reverencia predicte regule continenciam et paupertatem altissimam, que est in nichil habendo mundane in proprio vel communi, multiplicibus roboracionibus confirmarunt.
units.en: And so that the rule of blessed Francis might be shown truly to have come from God, and its professors need not fear to perish of want, the whole fabric of the world has many times been proved to serve that rule miraculously in aid of its poverty, as is more fully contained in his life approved by the Church. And so that it might appear plainly to those present and to come that the rule issued by blessed Francis and confirmed by the Church is truly the one that Christ taught the apostles and confirmed in himself by his example as to this article, Jesus Christ deigned to seal that same rule, in its author Francis, with the stigmata of his most holy passion. Hence, a few days having passed since the making of that rule, he was found worthy to be marked with the said stigmata, so that mortal man should not presume to overturn with a leaden bull what the immortal God reigning in heaven has established with the seals of his passion and cross. And all the Roman pontiffs, his predecessors, and several general councils confirmed with much devotion and reverence the content of the said rule and the highest poverty, which consists in having nothing in a worldly way, of one's own or in common, with manifold confirmations.
units.note: 'Bullare' is to seal with a bulla, the lead seal that gave papal letters their name: the stigmata are Christ's bull on the rule, and a 'leaden bull' cannot overturn it. 'A few days' compresses the dates: Honorius III approved the rule on 29 November 1223, and Francis received the stigmata on La Verna in September 1224 (Par. XI [9]).

units.orig: Hic autem oppressor pauperum et vite Christi et apostolorum inimicus predicta omnia parvipendens ac volens Christi paupertatem altissimam de medio tollere et sub miris dolis et fraudibus et venenatis fallaciis ipsam totaliter annullare, duo nephanda statuta, in quibus heresiarcha et hereticus perfectus cum aliis assercionibus alias factis notorie conprobatur et in Christi vitam plasphemus et sacris diffinicionibus sanctorum priorum pontificum predictorum aperte contrarius, promulgavit. Que constituciones ipsum sicut manifestum hereticum et de composicione ecclesie precisum incidisse in factum dampnatum hereseos et per consequens ab omni statu prelacionis depositum eiecerunt. Prima constitucio est promulgata per ipsum in Avinione, VI. Idus Decembris, millesimo trecentesimo vicesimo secundo, que incipit 'Ad conditorem'.
units.en: But this oppressor of the poor and enemy of the life of Christ and the apostles, making light of all this, and wishing to take the highest poverty of Christ out of the way and to annul it altogether under wondrous tricks and frauds and poisoned fallacies, promulgated two abominable statutes, in which, together with other assertions made elsewhere, he is notoriously proved a heresiarch and a perfect heretic, a blasphemer against the life of Christ and openly contrary to the sacred definitions of the holy earlier pontiffs named above. These constitutions have cast him out as a manifest heretic, cut off from the body of the Church, fallen into the condemned deed of heresy, and consequently deposed from every state of prelacy. The first constitution was promulgated by him at Avignon on the sixth day before the Ides of December, in the year 1322, and begins 'Ad conditorem'.
units.note: The sixth day before the Ides of December is 8 December 1322, the date of the first version of Ad conditorem canonum (Decr. Conditorem [1]); the second statute is Quum inter nonnullos of 12 November 1323 (Decr. Nonnullos [1]). The argument is the one Michael and later Ockham would make: a pope who contradicts a definition of faith by his predecessors is by that very fact a heretic, and so no longer pope; no court is needed to depose him.

units.orig: Quod eciam esse hereticum et vesanum, universitas fratrum Minorum in generali eorundem capitulo congregato Perusii aperte sensit et sentenciavit expresse asserendo, quod dicere Christum et apostolos nichil habuisse in communi non erat nec est hereticum, set sanum, katholicum et fidele et per sanctos patres summos pontifices tanquam katholicum diffinitum et contrarium reprobatum et tanquam reprobum excommunicacionis et anathematis sentencia innodatum. [...] Quod enim per clavem sciencie per Romanos pontifices semel determinatum est in fide et moribus recte vite, est inmutabile, eo quod ecclesia Romana est inerrabilis in fide et veritate nec potest dare regulam falsam vel malam in recte vivendo nec in veritatis iudicio ecclesia Romana potest sibi esse contraria. Si enim in uno esset falsa vel sibi contraria, in omnibus vacillaret. Et super hoc fundamento generale capitulum se in predicta littera stabilivit. Nam quod semel per summos pontifices Dei vicarios per clavem sciencie est diffinitum esse de fidei veritate, non potest per successorem aliquem in dubium revocari vel eius quod diffinitum est contrarium affirmari, quin hoc agens manifeste hereticus sit censendus. Cuius veritatis racio et fundamentum est, quia fides katholica est de vero perpetuo et inmutabili prorsus. Et ideo quod semel est diffinitum verum esse in ipsa fide vel moribus, in eternum verum est et inmutabile per quemcunque. Secus autem in hiis, que statuuntur per clavem potencie. Nam sepe quod uno tempore expedit fieri, alio tempore expedit prohiberi.
units.en: That this too is heretical and insane, the whole body of the Friars Minor, gathered in their general chapter at Perugia, plainly held and expressly pronounced, asserting that to say that Christ and the apostles had nothing in common was not and is not heretical, but sound, catholic and faithful, and was defined as catholic by the holy fathers, the supreme pontiffs, and its contrary rejected and, as rejected, bound with the sentence of excommunication and anathema. [...] For what has once been determined by the Roman pontiffs through the key of knowledge in faith and in the morals of right living is unchangeable, because the Roman Church cannot err in faith and truth, nor can it give a false or bad rule for right living, nor can the Roman Church contradict itself in judging the truth. For if it were false or self-contradictory in one thing, it would waver in all. And on this foundation the general chapter took its stand in the said letter. For what has once been defined by the supreme pontiffs, vicars of God, through the key of knowledge as belonging to the truth of faith, cannot be called into doubt by any successor, nor can the contrary of what was defined be affirmed, without the one who does so being judged a manifest heretic. The reason and foundation of this truth is that the catholic faith concerns what is true perpetually and wholly unchangeably. And therefore what has once been defined as true in the faith itself or in morals is true for ever and unchangeable by anyone. It is otherwise with what is ordained by the key of power. For often what it is expedient to do at one time, it is expedient to forbid at another.
units.note: The Perugia chapter of June 1322 and its letter 'dispersed throughout the world' (Chron. Perugia [2]) are here the ground of a theory of papal infallibility, invented to bind a living pope to a dead one: the key of knowledge defines and cannot be revoked; the key of power legislates and can. John XXII quoted this argument almost word for word in Quia quorundam (Decr. Quorundam [2]) and called it the teaching of the father of lies (Decr. Quorundam [1]). Schwalm notes that the bull answers the poverty chapters of this appeal and hardly anything else in it.

sections.blurb: The close, in the words of Philip IV's appeal against Boniface VIII: an oath that the charges are true and an appeal to a general council and to 'a true, lawful, future supreme pontiff'.

units.orig: Et ad sancta Dei ewangelia tacto libro iuravimus, omnia et singula supradicta nos credere vera esse, et quod de predictis talia probari poterunt contra eum, quod secundum statuta sanctorum patrum sufficienter sufficient ad eundem hereticum iudicandum. Iuramus eciam, nos pro viribus contra eundem prosecuturum predicta in concilio generali congregando in loco tuto atque securo ad honorem Dei et exaltacionem fidei christiane et sancte Dei ecclesie et sacri imperii [...].
units.en: And we have sworn on the holy gospels of God, touching the book, that we believe each and all of the above to be true, and that on these counts such things can be proved against him as will amply suffice, by the statutes of the holy fathers, to judge him a heretic. We swear also that we will pursue the above against him with all our strength in a general council to be gathered in a safe and secure place, to the honour of God and the exaltation of the Christian faith and of the holy Church of God and of the holy empire [...].
units.note: The oath, the call for a council and the appeal that follows are borrowed, often word for word, from the proceedings of Philip IV of France against Pope Boniface VIII in June 1303, the appeal of Guillaume de Nogaret and the king's protest, which Schwalm prints beneath the text ('Nos Philippus Dei gratia Francie rex …'). Schwalm marks further borrowings from the French dossier in chapters 31 to 33. 'Prosecuturum', singular for the royal 'we', is as printed.

units.titel: To a council and a lawful future pope
units.orig: [...] pro nobis et pro nobis adherentibus et nunc et in futurum adherere volentibus, cuiuscunque status et condicionis existant ecclesiastice vel mundane, ad predictum generale concilium, quod instanter et cum instancia repetita in loco tuto nobis et nostris convocari petimus, et ad verum legitimum futurum summum pontificem et ad sanctam ecclesiam matrem nostram et apostolicam sedem vel ad alios, ad quem vel ad quos fuerit appellandum, provocamus et appellamus in scriptis et appellationes per nos factas alibi innovamus et apostolos testimoniales a vobis principibus nostris ecclesiasticis et mundanis et notariis publicis hic presentibus cum instancia postulamus et iterum cum instancia postulamus.
units.en: [...] for ourselves and for those who adhere to us or wish to adhere now and in the future, of whatever state and condition they be, ecclesiastical or worldly, we provoke and appeal in writing to the said general council, which we ask urgently, and with urgency repeated, to be summoned in a place safe for us and ours, and to a true, lawful, future supreme pontiff, and to holy Church our mother and the apostolic see, or to any other or others to whom appeal must be made; and we renew the appeals made by us elsewhere; and we ask with urgency, and again with urgency, for testimonial apostoli from you, our princes ecclesiastical and worldly, and from the public notaries here present.
units.note: 'A true, lawful, future supreme pontiff': the reigning one is no longer counted. The chancery form (nr. 910) records that the appeals were read and lodged on 22 May 1324, around vespers, in the chapel of the house of the Teutonic Order at Sachsenhausen, across the Main from Frankfurt. Louis later said the chapter on poverty had been put in without his knowledge; Schwalm thought the friars' form may have been published more than once without the king. Four years later Michael of Cesena, having appealed at Avignon (Appeal [6]), fled to Louis at Pisa, and Ockham came with him.
